items.title: Louis Nelson Interview, 1960-04-18
items.q: I played with a fellow in Tippet-Owe by the name of Joseph Gabriel. They call him Gabriel, but some people say Gabriel, but we call him Gabriel. He was also, he had about a ten piece orchestra.

ctx.x: Any relation? No, no relation at all.

He was what you call a fellow, he couldn't see at night but he could just make out in the day. And he was a wonderful violin player. He used to come by my mother when we'd get new music like that. She'd play the melody on the piano and he had a real good ear, but he couldn't see the music at all. But he was a fine fellow. And then from there I played a couple of dates with Professor Clevon Williams and his band. Then later on, after I married, my son was born, I played with a fellow in Tippet-Owe by the name of…
Do you remember Lewis James, the bass player? Sure, sure. Was he from there? I think he told us.
